question.problem:
An environmental researcher is tracking the depth $d$, in meters, of a lake during a dry season. The following table shows the rate at which the depth is decreasing.

| **$t\,\text{(weeks)}$** | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ | $4$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${d}^{′}(t)\,\text{(meters/week)}$ | $-0.3$ | $-0.5$ | $-0.8$ | $-1.0$ |

At $t=2,$ the lake depth was $12$ meters. Use the tangent line approximation of $d$ at time $t=2$ to estimate the depth of the lake at $t=2.4.$ Do not round the answer.

The depth of the lake at $t=2.4$ weeks is estimated to be
{{field-1}}
meters.

current_example.problem: Suppose that $f(-2) = 0$ and $f'(-2)=2.$ Estimate the value of $f(-1.8)$ using the tangent line approximation of $f(x)$ at $x=-2.$
current_example.worked_solution:
The tangent line approximation to $f(x)$ at the point $a=-2$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}L(x) & =f(a)+{f}^{′}(a)(x-a) \\  & =f(-2)+{f}^{′}(-2)(x-(-2)) \\  & =0+2(x+2) \\  & =2(x+2).\end{aligned}
$$

We can approximate $f(-1.8)$ by evaluating the tangent line approximation at $x=-1.8.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-1.8) & ≈L(-1.8) \\  & =2(-1.8+2) \\  & =2(0.2) \\  & =0.4.\end{aligned}
$$
